title: Security posture discovery with Orchid Health
summary: Orchid Health did a security-first discovery to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main concerns: SOC 2 and ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs retention, and KMS integration for encryption and key control. Next steps: share SOC2 report, architecture diagram for Private deployment, schedule follow-up security deep dive with Orchid infra team, and provide a short pilot pricing estimate.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Lena Park (Redwood AE) - Share latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary - due 2026-04-02
Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE) - Draft architecture options for Private deployment (network diagram + KMS flow) - due 2026-04-06
Priya Shah (Orchid) - Send list of compliance questions and data residency requirements - due 2026-04-03
Ravi Kumar (Redwood) - Schedule 60-min security deep dive with Orchid infra/security team - due 2026-04-05
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and ISO artifacts
Redwood SE to produce Private deployment diagram with KMS/HSM options
Schedule technical security deep dive (60 min)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Head of Security, Orchid), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Ava Gomez (CTO, Orchid)

Auto-generated Summary: quick discovery on security posture; Orchid leaning toward private or dedicated for PHI workloads; needs SOC2/ISO evidence and KMS integration; wants RBAC and audit log retention details.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, excited to chat through your security questions. i think avi — ava — is hopping on a little late, but we have the core security folks which is great.
[00:18] Priya Shah: thanks lena, yes we wanted this call to focus squarely on compliance and ops — SOC2, ISO, SSO, encryption controls. we're evaluating hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and a private deployment. main use case will touch PHI so we need to understand the guarantees.
[00:35] Carlos Mendes: totally understood. quick intro from our side — i'm carlos, i lead infra integration at Redwood, and ravi here focuses on customer deployments. we can walk through evidence we have, how SSO/SAML works, RBAC options, and how key management and encryption would look for private installs.
[00:50] Marcus Lee: great. first high level question — does Redwood have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? our compliance matrix lists both as must-haves.
[01:04] Lena Park: yes — we have SOC 2 Type II. we also maintain an ISO 27001 summary and can share scope. we'll attach the reports after the call. note: for hosted, audited artifacts cover Redwood's control environment; for Private on-prem or VPC, you'll still get evidence for our control plane and will need to map customer-managed controls for the data plane.
[01:32] Priya Shah: ok, good. what about encryption at rest with customer-managed keys? we require KMS/HSM integration so that keys are in our control.
[01:45] Ravi Kumar: good question. for Dedicated and Hosted we support envelope encryption where you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) with cloud KMS providers; for Redwood Private, we have an option to integrate with customer KMS/HSM via KMIP or cloud KMS APIs. keys can be rotated per your policy; logs of key usage are available. crosstalk...
[02:07] Priya Shah: and for hosted, if we bring our KMS — do you still have access to plaintext?
[02:15] Carlos Mendes: short answer: no, not unless you explicitly allow it. with BYOK, the data plane still encrypts/decrypts in the environment but key access can be gated so Redwood-managed services do not retain long-term access to plaintext keys. for higher assurance, Private deployment puts the data plane within your VPC or on-premises so keys and crypto never leave your control.
[02:40] Ava Gomez: that aligns with what we expected. another thing — SSO: we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. can you integrate with our IdP and support just-in-time provisioning and role sync?
[02:56] Lena Park: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM. our Console integrates with SAML providers for login and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based and you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. for Dedicated and Private you can enforce stricter session timeouts and MFA via your IdP.
[03:18] Marcus Lee: for RBAC — do you support fine-grained roles? e.g., separate roles for devs that can call APIs vs ops that can view logs and audit trails?
[03:28] Carlos Mendes: yes — we provide pre-defined roles and custom roles. API keys can be scoped to routes/models and you can enforce least privilege. audit logs capture API key usage and admin actions.
[03:39] Priya Shah: audit logs — how long are they retained? we need 7 years for certain audits, though we know retention can be expensive; what's typical?
[03:50] Ravi Kumar: default retention for hosted logs is 90 days in the console; we offer extended retention as an add-on (1 year, 3 years). for Dedicated and Private, logs can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic) or S3 and retention is controlled by your policies. for Private on-prem the logs are entirely under your control.
[04:18] Priya Shah: perfect. do logs include request/response payloads? we need to redact PII/PHI in logs by default.
[04:27] Carlos Mendes: we redact sensitive payloads by default and have configurable masking rules. full payload capture is possible but we'd only recommend for controlled, internal audits and that must be agreed contractually with strict access controls.
[04:45] Ava Gomez: speaking of agreements, what's your breach notification and incident response SLA? we require 72-hour notification windows and support for evidence for incident response.
[04:58] Lena Park: our standard enterprise contract includes 72-hour breach notification. we also have a runbook and can provide incident response playbooks and a named security contact for escalation.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: on network side — for Private deployment, do you support air-gapped on-prem installs? we have some clinics that require no egress for certain workloads.
[05:22] Ravi Kumar: yes, we offer an air-gapped on-prem package for regulated customers. there are additional packaging and maintenance processes (offline updates, private images) but it's a supported offering.
[05:35] Priya Shah: do you do annual penetration tests and third-party vulnerability assessments?
[05:42] Carlos Mendes: we do annual pen tests, and monthly internal scans; results are summarized in our compliance pack. for customers that require direct access to raw reports, we can provide redacted findings or a customer-attested summary under NDA.
[05:58] Lena Park: just to align, sounds like Orchid's bar is SOC2 + ISO + BYOK/KMS + SAML/SCIM + long-term audit retention + air-gap option. is that fair?
[06:10] Priya Shah: yes that's a good summary. also we want RBAC that can map to our Okta groups and audit evidence to feed into our GRC.
[06:20] Ava Gomez: one commercial note — what's the cost delta between dedicated reserved capacity and private deployment? high-level is fine now.
[06:31] Carlos Mendes: high level: Dedicated is a predictable monthly commit for GPU pools; it's cheaper to adopt than a full Private on-prem because you don't bear infra ops. Private on-prem includes a platform license and support fee and sometimes professional services for deployment. we can follow up with ballpark numbers in the next email.
[06:52] Marcus Lee: any impact on latency/throughput with encryption BYOK?
[06:58] Ravi Kumar: negligible at inference time for envelope encryption; initial key exchange and occasional rotations are the only ops that have small cost. for strict HSM-backed signing paths, there can be a few ms of added latency during token ops but it's typically not material for inference.
[07:18] Priya Shah: what about data residency — some of our clinics must keep data in-state; do you support regionally isolated hosted deployments?
[07:28] Lena Park: yes; we can route requests to specific regions and for enterprise customers implement tenant isolation in a region. Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions; Private naturally satisfies residency when deployed on-prem or in your cloud account.
[07:45] Ava Gomez: any known customers doing PHI with Redwood we can reference?
[07:52] Lena Park: we have a few healthcare customers in our portfolio (we can share references under NDA). also, we've done pilots with some medtech companies and have healthcare-specific controls packaging.
[08:05] Priya Shah: regarding contractual terms — do you sign BAAs?
[08:11] Carlos Mendes: yes we can sign a BAA for PHI workloads. that's typically part of our enterprise contract for Dedicated or Private customers.
[08:20] Marcus Lee: excellent. let's dig into one architecture scenario — we want inference inline with our EMR pipeline; ideally models run in our VPC so nothing leaves network. how would that look?
[08:33] Ravi Kumar: for that scenario, Private deployment in your VPC is ideal. we'd deploy Redwood data plane components inside your subnet, integrate with your KMS, and provide a control plane (optional) hosted by Redwood or a customer-managed control plane depending on risk profile. network peering, private endpoints, and strict SG rules are used. we'll draw a diagram and share.
[08:58] Priya Shah: can you sketch the KMS flow — who holds keys and how are they used at inference time?
[09:06] Carlos Mendes: sure, high-level: keys live in your KMS/HSM; when a request needs decryption, the data plane requests a short-lived data key from the KMS; the KMS returns a wrapped data key which is used only in-memory by the data plane; keys are never written to disk; key usage logs are available from the KMS. we'll include a diagram in the follow-up.
[09:28] Lena Park: small note — for hosted BYOK there are nuances around backups and snapshots; we can document snapshot encryption and its lifecycle in the follow-up doc.
[09:41] Ava Gomez: ok. any limitations on model tooling in Private versus Hosted? like function calling, streaming, or batching?
[09:51] Carlos Mendes: feature parity is a goal. there may be minor differences depending on your infra and kernel support, but streaming, function/tool calling, batching are supported in Private; we'll call out any version-specific caveats in the diagram.
[10:07] Priya Shah: last question for now — regulatory certifications beyond SOC2/ISO, like HITRUST?
[10:14] Lena Park: we don't currently hold HITRUST out of the box, but we have customers that do HITRUST-level controls via Private deployments plus additional attestation. we can discuss what would be required if Orchid needs HITRUST specifically.
[10:28] Marcus Lee: perfect. should we recap next steps?
[10:33] Lena Park: yes — recap: we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, draft the Private deployment diagram with KMS flow, provide pilot cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private, and set up a 60-min security deep dive with your infra/security team.
[10:49] Priya Shah: thanks everyone, that timeline works for us. we'll send our compliance questionnaire to lena and carlos.
[10:56] Ava Gomez: thanks — appreciate the thorough answers.
[11:00] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with those artifacts by early next week. bye.

End of call.
